reasoning_content:
Interesting! The bullseye-security repository's package index lists curl 7.74.0-1.3+deb11u16, but that .deb has been deleted from the pool (404). The bullseye image was built on 2025-07-21, and since then (bullseye's security updates have stopped — bullseye LTS ended), newer curl versions published after the image build may have been deleted from deb.debian.org.

So even just installing curl from the bullseye repo fails due to pool deletions. The image's apt metadata is cached (from 2025-07-21). The security index may have been updated after that... hmm, actually `apt-get update` refreshed the index, and it now points to newer versions (deb11u16) whose .debs have been deleted from the pool.

Options:
1. Avoid needing curl in the image: use `apt-get download` (does apt also hit the same 404 pool? apt-get download fetches from the pool — yes, same 404).
2. Use python? Not installed. busybox wget? Alpine's busybox... this is Debian. Check if `wget` is available... no, neither.
3. Install the .deb without using apt: `dpkg -i`? The base image has dpkg. But pgrouting depends on postgresql-17 (installed), libpgrouting? Let me check the pgrouting deb's dependencies: postgresql-17-pgrouting-scripts, postgresql-17, postgresql-17-postgis, postgresql-17-postgis-scripts, libc6, libgcc-s1, libstdc++6. Are there any unmet dependencies? postgresql-17-pgrouting-scripts (all) — need to install this .deb too (with no dependencies other than postgresql-17-pgrouting? let me check). And libstdc++6 etc. are already installed. So `dpkg -i scripts.deb pgrouting.deb` might work without needing to download anything!

But how to download the .deb into the build? Without curl/wget in the image... Docker's build has no COPY from the host? Actually it can: put the .deb in the build context and COPY it in! The build context for db is ./postgres. Copy the .deb file into /workspace/deployment/postgres/ and COPY --from or a regular COPY in the Dockerfile. This works fine and is even verifiable: pre-download + sha256 on the host (already done: checksums verified), COPY to image, dpkg -i.

The .deb is 867KB + 67KB — no problem committing to the build context (it won't be committed to git; .gitignore probably... well, whatever, it's a local artifact).

Alternative: use `ADD https://...` in the Dockerfile — ADD supports remote URLs! `ADD <url> <dest>` downloads during the build. Then verify sha256sum in RUN. This avoids copying files into the build context. ADD http://... works with the dockerfile. Use ADD for both .debs, verify sha256, then dpkg -i.

This is cleaner. The Dockerfile becomes:

FROM postgis/postgis:17-3.5
ADD https://apt-archive.postgresql.org/pub/repos/apt/pool/main/p/pgrouting/postgresql-17-pgrouting-scripts_3.8.0-1.pgdg110+1_all.deb /tmp/...
ADD https://...postgresql-17-pgrouting_3.8.0-1.pgdg110+1_amd64.deb /tmp/...
RUN sha256sum -c ... && dpkg -i ... && rm ...

Does dpkg -i require the scripts .deb first? dpkg handles ordering: if you give it both files, dpkg will unpack both and configure. The main package Depends on the scripts package, so pass scripts first: `dpkg -i /tmp/...scripts.deb /tmp/...pgrouting.deb`.

Wait — do I even need to remove pgdg.list? If I don't run apt-get update anymore, leaving it is fine (no apt invocations). But the postgres entrypoint doesn't run apt. Leave the repo as is (harmless) — actually, if the container later runs apt-get update it'll fail, but nothing in this stack does that. Still, removing it is cleaner. Hmm, keep the change minimal: I only need the pgrouting extension file, so no apt is needed at all. Remove the broken repo list (to avoid confusing future apt invocations) and use ADD + dpkg.

Let me double-check: does postgresql-17-pgrouting depend on anything not installed? From the index:
Depends: postgresql-17-pgrouting-scripts (>= 3.8.0-1.pgdg110+1), postgresql-17, postgresql-17-postgis, postgresql-17-postgis-scripts, libc6 (>= 2.14), libgcc-s1, libstdc++6 (>= 9)
All satisfied (postgresql-17, postgis-3 installed; libc6 etc. standard). The scripts deb's dependencies? Let me check in the index — I'll grep it. Let me fetch its full entry.

Then rebuild db.

One more thing: ADD https:// — does docker allow http/https URLs with ADD? Yes, ADD supports http:// and https:// URLs (downloads into the image). In practice I've only used it with http, but https works too.

Let me update the Dockerfile.

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "cd /tmp && awk '/^Package: postgresql-17-pgrouting-scripts$/,/^$/' pg17_pkgs.txt", "summary": "Show full pgrouting-scripts package entry", "security_risk": "UNKNOWN"}
